title: The Universal Testimony Of The Cosmos 18th Degree 2nd Truth Mutual Assistance

questions.question: How does the passage describe what happens to the world in autumn and spring?
questions.answer: It says a world passes away in autumn and a new one appears in spring.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the world to help the reader understand this repeated coming and going?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a temporary lodging place where travelers stay for a while and then leave.

questions.question: In that comparison, what do the “travelers” represent?
questions.answer: They represent living beings and even whole realms that come, serve their purpose, and move on.

questions.question: What qualities of the Creator are said to be clear from this repeated order in the world?
questions.answer: His necessary existence, limitless power, and never-ending wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the regular pattern of death and renewed life support belief in power and wisdom?
questions.answer: Because such large-scale change happens in a measured, meaningful, and balanced way rather than randomly.

questions.question: According to the passage, for what kinds of purposes are these living realms used?
questions.answer: They are used for lordly purposes, Divine aims, and merciful ends.

questions.question: What does the passage say about contingence in relation to the universe?
questions.answer: It says contingence covers and surrounds all of creation.

questions.question: Which range of beings is included when the passage discusses contingence?
questions.answer: It includes everything from the highest created levels to the earth, and from tiny particles to huge heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What is meant by each thing being given a particular essence, form, identity, and attributes?
questions.answer: It means every created thing is made as a distinct and specified being, not as something vague or self-produced.

questions.question: Why is the selection of one form out of many possibilities important in the argument?
questions.answer: Because choosing one fitting form from countless options points to a deliberate chooser.

questions.question: How does the passage use the variety within a species to strengthen its point?
questions.answer: It says that giving each member its own fitting identity among many similar members shows intentional distinction.

questions.question: What does the passage say about assigning beneficial qualities and organs to creatures?
questions.answer: It presents that as evidence of wisdom, since those features are suitable and useful rather than accidental.

questions.question: What inference is made from creatures being specified in so many exact ways?
questions.answer: The inference is that a Necessary Existent determines and distinguishes all created things with perfect power and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s knowledge of things?
questions.answer: Nothing is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What does the comparison between creating spring, a tree, and a seed show?
questions.answer: It shows that great and small acts of creation are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How is contingence related to the larger testimony of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It is one of the two major supporting sides of that testimony.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the cosmos’s testimony “two-winged”?
questions.answer: Because it rests on two major truths: createdness and contingence.

questions.question: What is the overall conclusion of this passage about the universe?
questions.answer: The universe points clearly to one Creator whose existence is necessary and whose power and wisdom are unlimited.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the way death and new creation happen in nature?
questions.answer: They happen with order, regularity, and purpose.

questions.question: Why is the image of a traveler’s inn a meaningful comparison here?
questions.answer: It shows that worldly life is temporary and that beings come, stay briefly, fulfill a role, and depart.

questions.question: What does the ordered movement of these “travelers” imply about the One managing them?
questions.answer: It implies a majestic being who governs them intentionally and wisely.

questions.question: Which three Divine qualities are emphasized as especially obvious from this order?
questions.answer: Necessary existence, infinite power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: Besides power and wisdom, what else does the passage mention in describing the Creator’s action?
questions.answer: It mentions knowledge, balance, order, regularity, and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says these realms are employed for higher purposes?
questions.answer: It means they are not meaningless; they serve Divine and merciful goals.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the section on contingence?
questions.answer: All created things depend on being chosen and specified from many possible ways they could have been.

questions.question: How broad is the passage’s claim about this dependence on choice?
questions.answer: It applies to every level of creation, whether general or particular, large or small.

questions.question: What kinds of features in creatures are said to be selected?
questions.answer: Their essence, form, identity, qualities, and bodily equipment.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress the huge number of possible alternatives?
questions.answer: To show that landing on one exact and fitting arrangement cannot be explained by blind chance.

questions.question: What does the phrase about a creature being confused among many possibilities suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that created things do not determine themselves and need a determiner.

questions.question: How do useful organs function as evidence in the argument?
questions.answer: They show intentional design because they suit the creature’s life and benefit.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the exact specification of all beings?
questions.answer: A necessary and all-powerful Creator chooses and gives each thing its distinct reality.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about difficulty for the Creator?
questions.answer: Nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage illustrate that no task is harder for Allah than another?
questions.answer: By saying that making a whole spring is as easy for Him as making a tree, and making a tree is as easy as making a seed.

questions.question: In the structure of the argument, what role does contingence play?
questions.answer: It serves as one major part of the universe’s witness to its Creator.

questions.question: What main lesson should a careful reader take from the whole passage?
questions.answer: The detailed order and specification of the world point to Allah’s necessary existence, complete knowledge, perfect wisdom, and unrestricted power.

questions.question: What scene from nature introduces the main reflection in this passage?
questions.answer: The passing away of one seasonal world and the arrival of another.

questions.question: What two things are repeatedly joined together in the first paragraph of the passage?
questions.answer: Death and new creation.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the manner in which these repeated changes happen?
questions.answer: It describes them as highly orderly and regular.

questions.question: What does the lodging-place example teach about worldly existence?
questions.answer: It teaches that worldly existence is temporary and that beings are on a journey, not settled forever.

questions.question: What does it mean that worlds and realms “fulfill their duties”?
questions.answer: It means they serve assigned purposes before passing on.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the Creator’s existence is as clear as the sun to the intellect?
questions.answer: Because the large-scale order, balance, and purpose in creation strongly point to Him.

questions.question: What attributes of the Creator are linked with the making of “vital realms” and “purposive universes”?
questions.answer: Power, wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, regularity, and compassion.

questions.question: What transition does the passage make after discussing createdness?
questions.answer: It turns to the truth of contingence.

questions.question: In simple terms, what is contingence in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the fact that created things could have been otherwise and therefore depend on a chooser.

questions.question: What is the significance of every being having a particular essence?
questions.answer: It shows that each being is intentionally specified instead of existing necessarily by itself.

questions.question: How does the passage treat form and shape as part of its proof?
questions.answer: It argues that giving a fitting shape from countless possible shapes indicates deliberate selection.

questions.question: Why is distinct identity important in the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: Because it shows each being is singled out from among many similar possibilities.

questions.question: What do suitable qualities and useful organs reveal according to the passage?
questions.answer: They reveal wisdom and purposeful bestowal.

questions.question: How does the passage combine power and wisdom in its argument?
questions.answer: It presents exact creation as requiring both the ability to create and the wisdom to choose rightly.

questions.question: What does the statement that nothing is hidden from Him add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the Creator’s knowledge reaches every being without exception.

questions.question: Why is the comparison between spring and a seed especially powerful?
questions.answer: Because it joins the largest and smallest scales to show equal ease in creation.

questions.question: What metaphor is used for the cosmos’s witness to Allah?
questions.answer: It is described as a testimony with two wings.

questions.question: Which two truths make up those two wings in this passage?
questions.answer: Createdness and contingence.

questions.question: What natural process does the passage use to point beyond the world to its Maker?
questions.answer: The steady pattern of seasonal ending and renewal.

questions.question: What idea about the world is conveyed by calling it a stopping place for travelers?
questions.answer: The world is temporary, and its inhabitants are passing through rather than remaining permanently.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the movement of living realms and migrating worlds?
questions.answer: Their movement is directed and meaningful, not random.

questions.question: Which features of the world’s changes make them evidence rather than mere events?
questions.answer: Their balance, regularity, order, and purpose make them evidence.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from these observed patterns?
questions.answer: That there is a glorious Creator with necessary existence, boundless power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: How does mercy appear in the description of the Creator’s action?
questions.answer: The created realms are used for merciful goals and compassionate purposes.

questions.question: What broad claim does the passage make when beginning the section on contingence?
questions.answer: That contingence is present throughout the whole universe.

questions.question: Which extremes are mentioned to show the full scope of creation under this truth?
questions.answer: The highest created level and the earth, and also the atom and the planet.

questions.question: What does the passage say every created thing receives before entering the world?
questions.answer: It receives a specific essence, form, identity, qualities, and fitting organs.

questions.question: Why does the passage repeatedly mention “possibilities” and “probabilities”?
questions.answer: To stress how many alternatives there were before one exact outcome was chosen.

questions.question: What does choosing one exact identity among many members of a kind show?
questions.answer: It shows distinction by intentional will and knowledge.

questions.question: How does the passage portray creatures before they are given determined features?
questions.answer: It portrays them as lacking settled definition among many possible states.

questions.question: Why are beneficial organs important in the reasoning of the passage?
questions.answer: Because usefulness points to wise design, not accidental formation.

questions.question: What four kinds of specification are named near the end of the long sentence on contingence?
questions.answer: The specification of essence, identity, form, and condition or attribute.

questions.question: What does the passage infer about Allah’s relation to all beings, both universal and particular?
questions.answer: He creates, chooses, and distinguishes every one of them.

questions.question: What does the statement that no object is hidden from Him teach about Divine knowledge?
questions.answer: It teaches that His knowledge is complete and misses nothing.

questions.question: How does the passage connect size with ease in creation?
questions.answer: It says size makes no difference to Him; the biggest and the smallest are equally easy.

questions.question: What role does contingence play in the “great testimony” of the universe?
questions.answer: It functions as one supporting side of that testimony.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall inference a reader is supposed to draw from this passage?
questions.answer: The world’s constant renewal and exact specification of all things testify to one necessary, all-wise, all-powerful Creator.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what repeated event in the world is highlighted?
questions.answer: The repeated ending of one seasonal order and the appearance of another.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the world through the image of a place where travelers stay briefly?
questions.answer: It suggests that the world is not final or permanent for its inhabitants.

questions.question: What happens to the travelers in that image after they complete their work?
questions.answer: They move on.

questions.question: What does this image teach about the created realms of the world?
questions.answer: They are temporary, purposeful, and under management.

questions.question: Which Divine qualities are made evident by such management?
questions.answer: Necessary existence, infinite power, and unending wisdom.

questions.question: What additional features of Divine action are named alongside those qualities?
questions.answer: Knowledge, perfect measure, order, regularity, and compassion.

questions.question: What shift in topic occurs after the brief closing note on createdness?
questions.answer: The passage moves to the truth of contingence.

questions.question: What does it mean that contingence “surrounds” the cosmos?
questions.answer: It means everything in the universe shows dependence on being chosen and brought into a specific state.

questions.question: What levels of existence are included in this claim?
questions.answer: Every level, from the smallest to the largest and from individual things to broad categories.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is special about the essence of each thing?
questions.answer: It is a particular essence selected for that thing.

questions.question: What is the argument from form in this section?
questions.answer: A thing’s exact shape among many possible shapes points to a deciding Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage use identity as evidence?
questions.answer: It argues that giving each being its own distinct identity among many others requires choice and specification.

questions.question: Why do fitting qualities matter in the argument?
questions.answer: Because they show that creatures are given what suits them in a wise way.

questions.question: How do organs strengthen the passage’s claim?
questions.answer: They are useful and purposeful parts, so they indicate intentional equipping.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from all these precise selections?
questions.answer: A Necessary Existent creates and determines all contingent beings with unlimited power and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s awareness of creation?
questions.answer: Every object and every matter is fully known to Him.

questions.question: How does the example of spring, tree, and seed summarize the teaching about Divine power?
questions.answer: It shows that creating many things or few things, large things or small things, is equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe createdness and contingence as two wings?
questions.answer: Because together they carry the full witness of the cosmos toward recognition of the Creator.

questions.question: What broad phenomenon does the passage first ask the reader to notice in the world?
questions.answer: The repeated disappearance of one world-like order and the arrival of another through the seasons.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize about the way these seasonal changes occur?
questions.answer: They occur with striking order and consistency.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe the world’s temporary character?
questions.answer: It is pictured as an inn or lodging for those on a journey.

questions.question: In that metaphor, what is the significance of beings arriving, serving, and departing?
questions.answer: It shows they have assigned roles and do not remain by their own power.

questions.question: What does the passage say becomes obvious to the intellect through this scene?
questions.answer: The existence of a glorious Creator with absolute power and wisdom.

questions.question: Which aspects of the Creator’s governance are specifically mentioned?
questions.answer: Wise making, knowledgeable ordering, balance, regularity, and merciful purpose.

questions.question: After this, what truth is introduced as covering the whole universe?
questions.answer: The truth of contingence.

questions.question: How would you explain contingence in student-friendly language based on the passage?
questions.answer: It means created things are not necessary in themselves; they depend on being selected from many possible ways of existing.

questions.question: What examples of scale show that this truth applies everywhere?
questions.answer: It applies from the highest created levels down to earth, and from atoms up to planets.

questions.question: What five kinds of specification are listed for created things in this section?
questions.answer: Their essence, form, identity, attributes, and useful organs.

questions.question: Why is the idea of “many possible forms” central to the argument?
questions.answer: Because one exact fitting form being chosen points to intentional determination.

questions.question: How does the passage use the phrase about members of the same species?
questions.answer: It uses it to show that even among similar beings, each one is individually distinguished.

questions.question: What do wise qualities and beneficial organs reveal about the Creator?
questions.answer: They reveal His wisdom and purposeful care.

questions.question: What larger theological conclusion is drawn from the exact fitting of all these features?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that a Necessary Existent specifies all contingent beings.

questions.question: What does the statement that nothing is difficult for Him tell us about Divine power?
questions.answer: It tells us His power is unrestricted and not strained by complexity or size.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare creating a spring with creating a tree and a seed?
questions.answer: To show that for Allah, producing a vast system or a tiny being is equally effortless.

questions.question: In the cosmic testimony described here, what does contingence contribute?
questions.answer: It contributes one full side of the universe’s witness to its Creator.

questions.question: Taking the whole passage together, what is its main message for a reader reflecting on creation?
questions.answer: Creation’s recurring renewal and precise specification of every being point clearly to Allah’s necessary existence, total knowledge, perfect wisdom, and infinite power.
